subject: Startups
title: Valuation: Pre-Money vs. Post-Money
description: A fast breakdown of Valuation: Pre-Money vs. Post-Money for builders.

hook.text: A VC says: 'We'll invest $5M at $20M pre-money.' That means the post-money valuation is $25M and they own 20%.

buildup.text: Pre-money is the company's value before the investment. Add the investment amount and you get post-money.

discovery.text: YC's standard SAFE uses post-money valuation caps—$10M post means the investor gets 10% for a $1M investment.

climax.text: Pre-money valuation is what you negotiate. Post-money is what determines how much of the company you just sold.

punchline.text: Know the difference. One number could cost you millions.

quiz.question: If a company has a $20M pre-money valuation and raises $5M, what is the post-money valuation?
